title: Container Bookings: complete change account before goodwill on a customer roll fee
content:
## Rule
Goodwill on a Container Bookings customer roll fee is decided only on a complete change account: before a customer roll fee is waived, every change-of-destination fee and customer roll fee the booking owes must already be charged. The account is complete only when both of these hold:

| Condition | Meaning on the booking's ledger |
|---|---|
| No change of port of discharge on the booking is left without its change-of-destination fee. | the destination changes logged on the booking, less its change-of-destination fee entries, leave nothing over |
| No customer roll beyond the tier's free customer rolls is left without its customer roll fee entry. | the customer rolls beyond the free allowance, less the booking's customer roll fee entries, leave nothing over |

A change that owes no fee under its own rules does not leave the account incomplete. That is the case when the tier does not accept a change of port of discharge, when the tier charges no customer roll fee, or when no chargeable container is left once the containers of the booking's rejected dangerous-goods acceptance are left out, the chargeable containers being the booking's container count less the rejected acceptance's container count, never below zero.

## Cases (hypothetical ledgers)
*All figures are hypothetical inputs, for illustration only.*
- Tier accepts destination changes; one destination change logged, no change-of-destination fee entry; 5 chargeable containers: the account is **not** complete.
- Same ledger, but the tier does not accept a change of port of discharge: that change owes no fee, so it does not make the account incomplete.
- Tier allows 1 free customer roll; 3 customer rolls recorded and 2 customer roll fee entries: nothing is left over, so the roll side is complete.
- Tier allows 1 free customer roll; 3 customer rolls and 1 fee entry: one roll is left without its fee, so the account is **not** complete.
- A booking of 4 containers whose rejected dangerous-goods acceptance covers 4 containers: no chargeable container is left, so neither side leaves the account incomplete.
